findings.text: Provides firmware memory error translation into a machine check record. Descriptors lacking validated physical address are ignored. Granularity comes from an optional mask with page size fallback. A fresh record is prepared, marked as a memory read with unknown channel, loaded with the reported address, and handed to the logging path.

Severity controls extra marking on the synthesized record. Recoverable and higher adds uncorrected indication. Panic and higher additionally adds processor context corrupt indication and captures a timestamp. Bank uses a sentinel for none, while status combines validity, enablement, address and misc validity with a fixed read pattern, and misc encodes physical addressing plus granularity.
Initializes hardware error containers before use. The top level helper clears the container and then fills generic attributes plus per CPU attributes for the current processor.

Generic preparation captures processor identity, vendor, machine check capability and wall clock time through a deadlock safe accessor. Per CPU preparation captures logical and extended numbers, initial APIC identity, microcode revision, platform identifier and package identifier.
Central logging entry attempts pool insertion. Only on success it emits a notice that machine check events were logged and schedules deferred handling through interrupt safe work.

Pool insertion applies vendor filtering first and requires an initialized pool. Allocation failure is reported with rate limiting and treated as not logged. Success copies the full record into a pooled node and adds it to a lock free list.
Filtering dispatches on boot CPU vendor to AMD or Intel specific logic, accepting everything on other vendors. When vendor support is not built the corresponding filter is a constant accept.

AMD filtering drops records for three errata classes: disabled records on one early stepping, a specific extended code on fetch banks for a mid range family interval, and a translation error on one bank for older families. Bank classification comes from a helper described separately.

Intel filtering drops only bank zero records matching a fixed status pattern on a small set of Haswell, Broadwell and server Skylake variants linked to documented errata. All other records are accepted.
Bank type lookup is total and fails closed. Numbers beyond the supported maximum or banks without hardware identification return a sentinel meaning unknown type.
ACPI processor error entry simply forwards its context pointer and LAPIC identifier to the SMCA translator and returns that result.

SMCA translation validates prerequisites before touching state. It requires SMCA support, a start address matching the status register, a non empty register array, and a LAPIC identifier that matches some possible CPU. Any failure returns an invalid argument error.

On success the translator zeroes its container, fills generic and per CPU identity for the resolved CPU, derives bank from the reported address, caps consumption at fifteen registers, and populates status, address, misc, instance identity, syndrome and vendor syndromes from fixed array positions so shorter arrays fill only a prefix, then logs.

Observed encoding facts: granularity defaults to page shift absent mask validation; register count is array byte size divided by eight; bank comes from a middle address byte; at most fifteen registers are consumed in status first order.

Observed error record shape carries a nested machine check area with bank, status, misc, address, timestamp, syndrome and instance identity plus vendor syndrome storage, together with CPU identity fields for logical, extended, APIC, microcode, platform and package values.
Defines a static mutex for ACPI IOAPIC handling. No lock acquisition, ordering or protected data is visible in this lane.

Boot control globals cover ACPI enablement, IRQ and PCI skipping, LAPIC and IOAPIC presence, strictness, CMC distribution disable, legacy override tracking, SCI attributes, timer override policy, LAPIC address, and online capable support. Fragments show existence and documented initial values only.

Default facts observed: force flag cleared, interrupt model starts as legacy PIC, legacy ISA mapping is identity for sixteen lines, LAPIC address starts at the architectural default, SCI override uses an invalid sentinel, and override and feature flags start cleared.
Early table mapping returns null when address or size is zero and otherwise delegates to early remap; unmapping does nothing on null or zero size and otherwise delegates to early unmap.

MADT header handling requires APIC support and a mappable table. A non zero table address is adopted as LAPIC base, legacy compatibility is recorded when flagged, online capable accounting is enabled only on recent firmware revisions, and OEM specific driver matching is invoked last.

OEM selection walks registered APIC drivers and installs the first accepting the OEM identifiers. Installation ignores redundant installs, preserves the original completion handler, reapplies pending overrides, refreshes dispatched calls, adjusts maximum APIC identification when supported, and announces the chosen routing.

Override restoration and static call refresh apply to the same operation family covering completion, register access, inter processor signalling variants, controller register access and secondary wakeup, with static refresh additionally covering idle waiting.

Processor usability is true when enabled. Otherwise it follows the online capable flag when firmware support is present, else it treats disabled entries as usable only under non native hypervisors to support legacy guests.

Processor entry parsing validates length, skips sentinel identifiers and non usable entries, records that legacy entries were seen where relevant, and registers the remainder with topology. Extended entries additionally need build support, reject small identifiers when legacy CPUs exist, and validate identifiers before registration. One variant composes its identifier from two fields.

Topology registration rejects identifiers beyond the kernel limit, rejects the true bootstrap when a crash kernel is detected, and rejects non boot identifiers once the configured CPU limit is reached, counting each rejection. Accepted identifiers go to the internal registrar.

Bootstrap discovery avoids resetting the machine via misdirected initialization. It uses the hardware bootstrap indicator when available, trusts enumeration order otherwise, refuses to register a foreign bootstrap, constrains to one CPU when the boot identifier disagrees with hardware, and reports ordering violations as firmware bugs.

Internal registration marks present identifiers, assigns number zero to the boot identifier and otherwise reuses or allocates numbers persistently, stores APIC and ACPI identifiers and marks present, counts disabled entries, and updates membership maps for all topology domains with raw identifiers at the lowest level and masked identifiers above.

Address override parsing adopts the supplied LAPIC base unconditionally. Both extended and legacy non maskable interrupt parsers validate length and warn when the connection is not on line one, with no further state change visible here.

Parsing constants observed: all ones means invalid identifier, the 255 boundary separates legacy and extended identifier spaces, zero denotes the ISA bus, boot logs use an ACPI prefix, and a dedicated flag records that legacy processor entries were seen.
Legacy compatibility handling only records that dual PIC compatibility is present; no controller programming appears in this lane.

Observed firmware entry shapes carry APIC and ACPI identifiers with enablement flags for processor entries, an address for override entries, and a line number for non maskable interrupt entries, each with a length used for validation.
